t:
The Act of October 27, 1972 (86 Stat. 1308), is amended—

    (1) in subsection 3(b) by deleting the word “constructed” and by adding at the end thereof: “To inform the public of the contributions of Representative Ryan to the creation of the recreation area, the Secretary shall provide such signs, markers, maps, interpretive materials, literature, and programs as he deems appropriate. Not later than December 31, 1980, the Secretary shall take such additional actions as he deems appropriate to recognize and commemorate the contributions of Representative Ryan to the recreation area.”; and
 
    (2) in subsection 4(b), by changing “eleven members” in the first sentence to “fifteen members” and by changing “three members” in paragraph (5) to “seven members”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a technical amendment plus one-way public information (signs and markers about Representative Ryan), which is not participation. But the 1972 Act (86 Stat. 1308) is the Gateway National Recreation Area statute, and from background knowledge its subsection 4(b) sets the membership of the area's Advisory Commission, with paragraph (5) covering general-public members. Enlarging that commission from eleven to fifteen members expands a body of non-federal members that advises the Secretary. The section itself never names the commission, so this reading relies on knowledge of the underlying Act and is uncertain.
fable.s: in subsection 4(b), by changing “eleven members” in the first sentence to “fifteen members” and by changing “three members” in paragraph (5) to “seven members”

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to provide informational materials to the public, which is a one-way communication from the government to the public, not a consultation or coordination process involving outside parties in a decision. The amendment to the membership numbers of a board does not specify that the members are non-federal or that the board serves an advisory role involving outside participation; without evidence that the board includes non-federal members or engages in public consultation, it is treated as an internal government structure. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.
qwen_block.s: To inform the public of the contributions of Representative Ryan to the creation of the recreation area, the Secretary shall provide such signs, markers, maps, interpretive materials, literature, and programs as he deems appropriate.

opus.w: Subsection 4(b) of the Act of October 27, 1972 (the Golden Gate National Recreation Area Act) appears to set up the recreation area's Advisory Commission, whose members represent local governments and the general public. Increasing its membership expands an advisory body of non-federal members, which counts as participation. The tempting 'No' reading looks only at the commemorative signage in part (1), which is not participation, but part (2) restructures an outside advisory body.
opus.s: in subsection 4(b), by changing “eleven members” in the first sentence to “fifteen members” and by changing “three members” in paragraph (5) to “seven members”
opus.b:
I labelled this **Yes**, with moderate confidence (0.6), because part (2) appears to enlarge a body that includes non-federal members.

**The tempting-but-wrong reading:** Part (1) is the most obvious content, and it is not participation. It only tells the Secretary to put up signs, markers and interpretive materials honoring Representative Ryan. Taken alone, the section would look like a "No."

**Why part (2) points to "Yes":** It changes "eleven members" to "fifteen members" in subsection 4(b) of the 1972 Act. Based on my background knowledge, which I have not checked against the 1972 text, that Act is the Golden Gate National Recreation Area statute. Its member-based body is an Advisory Commission whose members come from local-government recommendations and represent the general public. If that is right, the amendment expands an advisory commission of non-federal members, which counts under the definition. The worked examples also treat commissions and boards as participation even when their makeup is not spelled out.

**Main uncertainty:** The section never names the body or describes its members. The "Yes" depends on my recollection of what subsection 4(b) of the 1972 Act creates, and I am unsure which section number holds the commission.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to provide information to the public (signs, markers, etc.), which is a one-way communication and does not involve consulting or coordinating with the public before making a decision. The other part of the section changes the number of members on a board but does not specify that these members are outside the federal government or that they participate in decision-making in a way that involves external consultation. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: To inform the public of the contributions of Representative Ryan to the creation of the recreation area, the Secretary shall provide such signs, markers, maps, interpretive materials, literature, and programs as he deems appropriate.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "informing the public" constitutes participation because it involves the general public. However, the definition of participation requires that the government *consult* or *coordinate* with outsiders *before* making a decision, or that outsiders have a role in an advisory body or decision-making process. Merely providing information to the public (one-way communication) does not involve the public in the decision-making process itself. The section describes commemorative actions (signs, markers) and administrative changes to a board's size, but does not mandate that the public or any outside group provide input that influences a federal decision. The board mentioned in subsection (2) is likely an internal or statutory board, and changing its size does not inherently create a participation mechanism with outsiders unless the board's composition is specified to include non-federal members (which is not stated here, only the number changes). The primary action is the Secretary providing information *to* the public, not consulting *with* them.
